metaDescription: UPL LB1 lima bean is a lima bean variety. About 73 days to harvest, 9.4 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: UPL LB1 is a registered lima bean variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1979. UPLB bred it. It takes about 73 days from sowing to harvest, with 9.43 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about UPL LB1 lima bean
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

UPL LB1 lima bean takes about 73 days from sowing to harvest. That is 4 days longer than the average of the 5 lima bean varieties with a day count, 69 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 9.43 t/ha trails the average of its group, 10.18. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 73 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It was weak against anthracnose, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit lima bean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
The seed coat is brown seeded.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Dark green pods, medium brown seeds.
Strongly determinate, erect bush about 46 cm tall (no trellis).
Highly susceptible to anthracnose, moderately resistant to fusarium.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: uPLB bush type lima bean on the Seed Board list, current seed sellers not confirmed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant UPL LB1 lima bean

Patani climbs and bears for a long time. Pick a variety by seed size and color, and give it a strong trellis. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 73 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 9.43 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of UPL LB1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
